content: Goal: orient in the workspace before proposing an idea. Action: list_directory on the workspace root. Observed: see listing result. Reasoning: need to check what mechanisms already exist so the proposal does not copy them, and aim at a coupling position not covered by earlier rounds (Frechet successor codebook, feedback-curvature control, radial Poincare assignment). Open: identify repo code for RQ-VAE / Stage2-Stage3 to check novelty.

Goal: choose a coupling position not used by the three earlier rounds (successor-weighted Fréchet codebook update; per-level curvature from prefix-transition score; entropy→radial Poincare rank) nor by the probe names (behcone-prefix-rq, Lorentz-succprofile-smooth-RQ, TSG-SID, succboost-geoshift, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ). Action: listed workspace (only progress.jsonl, no repo code available), reasoned over design space. Decision: move the coupling from the codebook/curvature/radius to the FRAME of the residual chain - a behaviour-derived base point (popularity-adjusted PMI successor Lorentz barycentre) at which log/exp maps are taken, so every RQ level's residual digit is expressed in a successor frame. Curvature fixed K=-1 Lorentz model; operators log_b/exp_b; reconstruction loss is geodesic arcosh distance. Switches: behaviour-off => base point = origin (plain hyperbolic RQ-VAE); geometry-off => Euclidean base point/midpoint plus L2 residual and loss. No ablation arm is trained; switches exist only in code. Identifier: SAC-LRQ. Cost estimate: anchor refresh O(nnz*(d+1)) once per epoch (3000 refreshes), per-step 1023 items x 4 exp/log over 33 dims (<2% flops of encoder, ~10-20% wall clock), anchor table 24556x33 floats ~3.2MB, zero cost at Stage 3 because anchors are training-only. Open: nothing blocking; full answer written next.

IDEA: SAC-LRQ
TITLE: Successor-anchored Lorentz residual quantization: every RQ digit is expressed in the training-behaviour successor frame, not at the origin
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender decodes a prefix of SIDs and must predict the next item; but RQ prefix digits are learned from item content alone, so the first digit mostly says "what this item looks like", not "which continuation it belongs to". Items that share continuation structure (same successor community) land in different prefixes, and prefix-conditioned decoding is therefore weakly informative. The problem addressed is to make the whole prefix hierarchy speak the language of the transition behaviour while staying a single, trainable, curved quantizer.
NOVELTY: Earlier work here changed the codebook update (successor-weighted Frechet codebook), the curvature per level (prefix-transition feedback curvature), or the radial rank of assignment (entropy-ranked radius), and there are cone/profile/transport variants. None of them moves the ORIGIN of the residual chain. SAC-LRQ keeps the RQ-VAE codebook update, the codebook size and the level count untouched, and instead makes the base point of the tangent-space residual chain a training-behaviour Lorentz barycentre of popularity-adjusted successor PMI neighbours. The SID becomes "displacement of the item from the centroid of what typically follows its predecessors", so all L levels (not only level 1) are relative to behaviour. It is not a behaviour suffix on a Euclidean quantizer: the assignment, the residual recursion, the reconstruction and the loss all change coordinate chart, and the chart itself is a curved (exp/log at a data-dependent point) object.
CHANGE: Replace h_i = exp_0(E(i)) with a residual chain that starts at the behaviour anchor a_i and writes h_i = exp_{a_i}(sum_l e_{l,k_l}), with per-level codes chosen by Euclidean distance in the tangent frame T_{a_i}; the codebook is shared and updated exactly as before, but its digits now mean successor-frame offsets, and the reconstruction loss is the geodesic distance on the hyperboloid.
SPECIFICATION: Curvature fixed K = -1 (Lorentz model L^d = {h in R^{d+1}: <h,h>_L = -1, h_0>0}, <u,v>_L = -u_0 v_0 + sum_{a=1..d} u_a v_a). Encoder E(i) in R^d gives tangent vector z_i at the origin. exp_0(z) = (sqrt(1+||z||^2), z); log_0(h) = h_{1:}/(h_0+1). For a base point b on L^d and u in T_b: exp_b(u) = cosh(||u||) b + sinh(||u||) u/||u||; log_b(h) = (arcosh(alpha)/sqrt(alpha^2-1)) (h - alpha b) with alpha = -<b,h>_L. Behaviour anchor: from training-split directed counts N_ij (consecutive item pairs inside training sessions), r_i = sum_j N_ij, c_j = sum_i N_ij, T = sum_ij N_ij, edge weight w_ij = max(0, log(N_ij T/(r_i c_j))) (PMI, positivity threshold at 0, no tuned constant), v_ij = w_ij / sum_j w_ij, a_i = normalize_L( sum_j v_ij h_j ) with h_j = exp_0(E(j)) detached, normalize_L(s) = s / sqrt(max(eps, -<s,s>_L)). Isolated items (sum_j w_ij = 0) use a_i = normalize_L(sum_j h_j), the global item barycentre. Anchors are refreshed once per epoch (precomputed table, no_grad) and are read-only inside the step. Then, per item: u_0 = log_{a_i}(h_i); for l = 1..L: k_l = argmin_k ||u_{l-1} - e_{l,k}||_2^2, u_l = u_{l-1} - e_{l,k_l}; h_hat = exp_{a_i}(u_L); loss = mean( arcosh(clamp(-<h_hat,h_i>_L, min=1+1e-6))^2 ) + beta * mean( sum_l ||sg(u_{l-1}) - e_{l,k_l}||_2^2 ). beta = 0.25 (documented RQ-VAE default), codebooks updated by EMA with decay 0.99 (documented default), codebook ini

t N(0, sigma^2) with sigma = median_i ||log_{a_i}(h_i)|| measured on the first epoch's first batch (derived, not searched). Diagnostics recorded but never gating: prefix-conditioned successor entropy on held-out training transitions, prefix/community adjacency, transfer predictability, ER/prefix counts/collisions. Stage 3 protocol unchanged and SIDs are frozen after Stage 2, so no anchor is needed at decode time.
COST: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch so about 1023 items per step, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): per step one anchor gather of 1023 x (d+1) (d=32 -> 33 floats) plus 4 exp/log-map evaluations per item per level with L=3, i.e. about 1023 x 12 maps over 33 dimensions, roughly 0.5-1 MFLOP and 3-4 extra elementwise passes over a 1023 x 33 buffer - under 2 percent of the encoder forward FLOPs, estimated 10-20 percent Stage 2 wall-clock (the arcosh/sinh calls dominate and vectorise). Anchor refresh costs O(nnz(T)*(d+1)) = about 1-2 x 10^7 FLOPs per epoch (nnz of the training transition graph, order 2-5 x 10^5), milliseconds, done 3000 times: negligible. Memory: 24556 x 33 float32 = 3.2 MB for the anchor table, plus the same table twice if double-buffered. Zero extra Stage 3 cost: anchors are training-only, generated SIDs are just integers.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping iff the successor frame makes prefix digits behaviour-decisive rather than merely content-decisive, i.e. the same first digit is shared by items whose successor distributions overlap, the prefix-conditioned successor entropy drops relative to the frozen baseline tokenizer, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observed through the recorded prefix/successor diagnostics and the single Stage 3 recall number.
RISKS: Hub items pull anchors toward the global barycentre (PMI weighting damps it, but a very skewed graph could make many a_i nearly collinear, degenerating the frame); reconstruction targets far from their anchor can push codebooks to the ball boundary and saturate (mitigated by the tangent-space assignment and by the arcosh clamp); encoder drift makes epoch-stale anchors inconsistent with live embeddings (detach plus one-epoch lag, a known small bias); the 1/2-free successsor frame could reduce absolute-semantic prefix sharing and hurt generative decoding if the decoder prefers content-regular prefixes; a single run with seed noise can hide a real improvement, which is accepted by programme policy.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions (successor PMI graph), used as the per-item successor barycentre; the signal is the directed 1-hop transition count matrix with row/column popularity normalisation.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage 2 TRAINING split only: within each training session, count consecutive ordered item pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) into N_ij, restricted to the 24556 training item vocabulary; discard pairs whose source or target is out-of-vocabulary; build N once before Stage 2 training and freeze it (no count update during training). At the start of each epoch compute a_i from the frozen N and from the current (detached) encoder embeddings; store the anchor table. No validation or test sessions are read.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: N is built exclusively from Stage 2 training interactions; validation and test sessions are never touched in building N, in computing the anchors, or in any diagnostic used to construct SIDs; the anchor table is a pure function of training counts and training-split e

mbeddings, refreshed before the validation-free Stage 2 training step. SIDs are frozen after Stage 2, so Stage 3 decoding cannot route any test interaction back into SID construction, and no test item's neighbours enter the graph because out-of-vocabulary and non-training edges are dropped.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature K = -1 Lorentz/hyperboloid model: exponential and logarithmic maps at a data-dependent base point (exp_b, log_b), Lorentz normalization, and the geodesic distance d_L(x,y) = arcosh(-<x,y>_L) used as the reconstruction loss. No curvature is trained, so there is no curvature constant to tune.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the RQ-VAE quantization itself, i.e. in the residual recursion (u_0 = log_{a_i}(h_i)), in the level-to-level residual update, in the reconstruction (h_hat = exp_{a_i}(u_L)) and in the Stage 2 reconstruction loss. It therefore acts in every training step of Stage 2, not as a side loss.
COUPLING PATH: One path: training transition counts -> PMI successor weights -> Lorentz barycentre a_i -> base point of log/exp maps -> residual chain and geodesic reconstruction loss -> gradients into the encoder and codebooks. Removing the behaviour sets a_i to the origin (residual chain at a fixed origin becomes plain hyperbolic RQ-VAE); removing the geometry makes the base point a Euclidean midpoint with L2 residuals and L2 loss. Either removal changes the numbers the level-1 assignment sees, so the two are not separable.
COUPLING EQUATION: a_i = Normalize_L( sum_j v_ij(N) * h_j ), v_ij(N) = max(0, log(N_ij T/(r_i c_j))) / sum_j max(0, log(N_ij T/(r_i c_j)));  u_0 = log_{a_i}(h_i);  e*_{l} = argmin_k || u_{l-1} - e_{l,k} ||_2^2 with u_l = u_{l-1} - e_{l,k_l};  h_hat = exp_{a_i}(u_L);  L = d_L(h_hat, h_i)^2 = arcosh(-<exp_{a_i}(u_L), h_i>_L)^2. The behaviour term enters only through a_i (and hence through the log/exp base), the curved term is exp/log/d_L; the equation is a single chain with no additive side term.
OBSERVABLES: (1) SID assignment: items with overlapping successor distributions (PMI neighbourhood Jaccard above 0) should share the first prefix digit more often than under the origin-anchored tokenizer, and first-digit groups should have lower successor entropy; (2) parameter update: gradients to the encoder now pass through log_{a_i} and exp_{a_i}, so per-item encoder gradient norms correlate with d_L(a_i, h_i); (3) prefix behaviour predictability: train-split P(successor community | prefix) sharpens monotonically with prefix length; (4) Stage 3 test_recall@10, the judgement, above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: a_i := origin of the Lorentz model for every item (behaviour switch false), which makes u_0 = log_0(h_i) and h_hat = exp_0(u_L): a plain hyperbolic RQ-VAE with the same codebooks, curvature, encoder and loss. The switch exists as a single boolean consumed where the anchor table is selected; no such arm is trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: replace exp_b/log_b/d_L by their Euclidean counterparts (b_i = (h_i + a_i)/2, u_0 = h_i - b_i, h_hat = b_i + u_L, loss = ||h_hat - h_i||^2), keeping the behaviour anchors and the behaviour weights identical. The switch exists as one geometry enum consumed by the quantization module; no such arm is trained in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the coupled run described above - PMI successor Lorentz barycentre anchors and hyperbolic exp/log residual recursion with geodesic loss - trained once on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs, 24 steps per ep

och, four cards, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
SPEC EQUATIONS: exp_0(z) = (sqrt(1+||z||^2), z); log_0(h) = h_{1:}/(h_0+1); exp_b(u) = cosh(||u||) b + sinh(||u||) u/||u|| ; log_b(h) = (arcosh(alpha)/sqrt(alpha^2-1))(h - alpha b), alpha = -<b,h>_L ; ||u|| = sqrt(max(0, <u,u>_L)) ; d_L(x,y) = arcosh(max(1+1e-6, -<x,y>_L)). Pseudocode: 1) build N from training sessions, freeze; 2) each epoch: for all items h_j = exp_0(E(j).detach()); s_i = sum_j v_ij h_j; a_i = s_i/sqrt(max(1e-8, -<s_i,s_i>_L)); cache A; 3) each step, batch B: h_i = exp_0(E(i)); b_i = A[i]; u = log_{b_i}(h_i); acc = 0; for l in 1..L: k_l = argmin_k ||u - e_{l,k}||^2; acc += e_{l,k_l}; u = u - e_{l,k_l}; h_hat = exp_{b_i}(acc); loss = mean(arcosh(clamp(-<h_hat,h_i>_L,1+1e-6))^2) + 0.25*mean(sum_l ||sg(u_{l-1}) - e_{l,k_l}||^2); 4) EMA-update codebooks; 5) after epoch 3000, emit SIDs (k_1,...,k_L) through the same chain with detached anchors, then run the frozen Stage 3 protocol.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: item indices of a training batch, encoder embeddings E(i) in R^d, frozen PMI transition counts N, current codebooks {e_{l,k}}, curvature K=-1, booleans use_behaviour and use_hyperbolic. Intermediate: anchor table A in R^{n x (d+1)} refreshed per epoch, base points b_i, tangent residual u_{l-1}. Outputs: per item the SID tuple (k_1..k_L) in {1..K}^L, the reconstructed point h_hat on L^d, and the scalar loss whose gradient updates encoder and codebooks.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp -<x,y>_L to at least 1+1e-6 before arcosh; use the series form arcosh(alpha)/sqrt(alpha^2-1) -> 1 for alpha close to 1 to avoid 0/0 in log_b; guard ||u|| with max(norm, 1e-8) and use u/||u|| -> 0 when the norm is below 1e-8; Lorentz-normalise every produced point with sqrt(max(1e-12, -<s,s>_L)) and reject/clamp points whose time coordinate is not positive; zero-weight rows fall back to the global item barycentre; renormalise codebooks after the EMA update so codes stay finite and the tangent frame does not blow up; PMI weights use the max(0, log(...)) threshold so no tuned smoothing constant is introduced; anchors are detached and refreshed only per epoch to keep the quantizer target stationary within a step; the commitment weight (0.25) and EMA decay (0.99) are documented RQ-VAE defaults, and the codebook init scale is a measured median, so no hyperparameter is chosen by trial.
END IDEA
